{"id": "9a15d492-52cd-4d43-a2c1-4003b00db440", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "This confirms the picture — Q Apps sits on top of Q Business with its own, separate permission and feature-enablement surface, so "IAM and Identity Center check out" for regular chat doesn't mean they check out for Q Apps specifically. Here's where to look:

**1. Missing `qapps:*` IAM permissions (most likely culprit)**
The web experience/user role needs explicit Q Apps actions — `qapps:*` (or granular actions like `CreateQApp`, `CopyQApp`, `CreateLibraryItemReview`, etc.) — on top of `qbusiness:*`. A role that's fully scoped for Q Business chat can still 403 on Q Apps because these are a distinct action namespace. Check the web experience's IAM role (or the user's federated role) for `qapps:*`.

**2. Q Apps also typically requires `quicksight:*` in the same role**
AWS's own setup guidance pairs `qapps:*` with `quicksight:*` permissions for the web experience role — Q Apps uses QuickSight under the hood for some rendering/data features. A role with `qapps:*` but missing `quicksight:*` can still throw 403s on certain Q Apps actions.

**3. Q Apps feature toggle not enabled on the application**
Independent of IAM, Q Apps is an admin-controlled feature flag on the Q Business application itself ("admin controls and guardrails"). If an admin hasn't explicitly enabled "Q Apps" for the application environment, every user — regardless of IAM or Identity Center assignment — gets blocked, since the capability is off at the app level, not the user level.

**4. Identity Center app assignment granularity**
Identity Center "assignment checks out" usually means the user has access to the Q Business application in general. But Q Apps can be gated by an additional access scope/grant on the Identity Center-managed application (`sso:PutApplicationAccessScope` configuration) — worth confirming the Q Apps scope specifically was included when the application was set up, not just base chat access.

**Suggested order of checks:**
1. Confirm Q Apps is enabled in the Q Business application's admin feature settings.
2. Inspect the IAM role attached to the web experience (or the user's IAM Identity Center-federated role) for `qapps:*` actions.
3. Check for `quicksight:*` permissions alongside it.
4. If all three look right, check the Identity Center application's access scopes for a Q Apps-specific grant.

If you want, I can pull the actual IAM role/policy attached to this user's Q Business web experience and check for the `qapps:*`/`quicksight:*` actions directly — just point me at the account/region and application ID.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
